prompt: A documentation site changes a few times a week and is the same for every visitor.
tells: changes a few times a week
why: Pre-render at build time and serve static files.
trap: Rendering on every request does the same work over and over.

prompt: A marketing blog should load instantly worldwide with no servers to scale.
why: Static pages can be served from anywhere, cheaply.

prompt: An online store has 2 million product pages. Rebuilding them all on each price change takes hours.
why: Use incremental static regeneration: rebuild pages on demand or on a timer.
trap: Still static, just not all at once.

prompt: A public changelog page updates only when a release ships, which triggers a deploy anyway.
tells: updates only when a release ships
why: If content only changes with a deploy, build it then.
trap: Server rendering adds cost for no freshness gain.

prompt: Fifty campaign landing pages change only when marketing edits them in the CMS, which can trigger a rebuild.
tells: change only when marketing edits them
why: Build them ahead of time; a CMS webhook rebuilds on edit.
trap: Nothing differs per visitor or per request.

prompt: A conference site lists talks from a JSON file in the repo. Every visitor sees the same schedule.
tells: Every visitor sees the same schedule
why: Data known at build time means pages can be built ahead.
trap: No server work is needed per request.

prompt: A side project must stay on free static hosting with no server runtime at all.
why: Static output is the only option without a server.
trap: SSR needs something running per request.

prompt: A static jobs board shows postings that closed hours ago, because it only rebuilds nightly.
why: Rebuild more often or on-demand (ISR) when postings change.
trap: The fix stays static; just regenerate sooner.
